div.head: Ps Cn for 21.2
div.ab: nam crimen ueneris ab antiquo inter maiora et non immerito numerabatur, uiridis uero, fractione chacee nostre regalis excepta, ita pusillum et exiguum est, quod uix ea respicit nostra constitutio; qui in hoc tamen deliquerit, sit criminis foreste reus.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 623 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: for the crime of venison was from of old, and not undeservedly, counted among the greater [crimes], but [that] of vert, except for breach of our royal chase, is so small and slight that our ordinance scarcely regards it; yet whoever offends in this, let him be guilty of a forest crime.

note.seg: vielleicht kannte Verf. die German. [und wohl auch Angelsächs.] Auszeichnung des Diebstahls an Wild (Brunner II 639), wenn er — wie das 12. Jh. meist; vgl. o. S. 614g — als alte Zeit die vor 1066 meint

Perhaps the author knew the Germanic [and probably also Anglo-Saxon] special treatment of theft of game (Brunner II 639), if — as the 12th century mostly does; compare above p. 614 note g — he means by 'ancient times' the time before 1066

chacea, auch 27,2. 28 ff., muss, ohne Beziehung auf captio (Jagd), umhegten Wald — wie Engl. chase — bedeuten, fractio regalis chaceæ einen Waldfrevel bestimmter Schwere und die feste Busse dafür, so laut 27, 2 die Tödtung auch ungeschützter Thiere, wenn sie innerhalb des Königsforstes geschah, laut 28 f. Holzfällung auch nicht fruchttragender Bäume, aber laut dieser Stelle nicht leichteren Baumfrevel oder Weidefrevel. Auch Ralf Niger scheidet uirgas colligere von syluestria in agriculturam agere, dem Essart; ed. Anstruther p. 168. Im reguardum von 1229 (ed. Shirley Royal letters I 347) steht chacie regis, wo Heinrichs II. Assise (Rog. Hov. II 244) defense (Eingehegtes) gesagt hatte

chacea, also 27,2. 28 ff., must mean, without reference to captio (hunting), enclosed wood — like English chase —, and fractio regalis chaceæ an offence against the forest of a certain gravity and the fixed fine for it: thus according to 27, 2 the killing even of unprotected beasts if it happened within the king's forest, according to 28 f. the felling even of non-fruit-bearing trees, but according to this passage not lesser offences against trees or pasture. Ralf Niger too distinguishes uirgas colligere from syluestria in agriculturam agere, the assart; ed. Anstruther p. 168. In the reguardum of 1229 (ed. Shirley Royal letters I 347) chacie regis stands where Henry II's Assize (Rog. Hov. II 244) had said defense (enclosed land)

Im 13. Jh. hat chacea die technische Bed.: ‘Privaten überlassener Forst’ (Turner p. cix), hier offenbar noch nicht. — Nur vor viridarii und forestarii, aber nicht vor die Reiserichter kamen die Klagen wegen Holzschlag im Forst im 13. Jh.; Turner p. xxxiii ff.

In the 13th century chacea has the technical meaning ‘forest left to private persons’ (Turner p. cix), here evidently not yet. — In the 13th century complaints about felling wood in the forest came only before the viridarii and forestarii, not before the itinerant justices; Turner p. xxxiii ff.
